subject: Accounting
title: Debits and Credits Explained
description: A quick win: understand Debits and Credits Explained.

hook.text: Debit doesn't mean bad. Credit doesn't mean good. They're just two sides of every transaction.

buildup.text: Debits increase asset and expense accounts. Credits increase liability, equity, and revenue accounts.

discovery.text: When you buy supplies with cash, you debit supplies (up) and credit cash (down). Balance kept.

twist.text: The terms are counterintuitive at first—a bank 'credits' your account, but in your books it's a debit.

climax.text: Once you understand the pattern, every transaction follows the same logic—debit one, credit another.

punchline.text: Debit left. Credit right. Balance always.

quiz.question: What does a debit do to an asset account?

details.summary: Debits and credits are the two-sided recording system that forms the foundation of double-entry bookkeeping. This topic demystifies which accounts get debited, which get credited, and why the system always balances.
details.whyItMatters: Every bookkeeping transaction requires understanding debits and credits. Misunderstanding them leads to incorrectly recorded transactions, unbalanced books, and unreliable financial statements.
takeaways: Debits increase assets and expenses; credits increase liabilities, equity, and revenue
Every transaction must have equal total debits and credits to keep the books balanced
Debits are not bad and credits are not good—they are simply left-side and right-side entries

faq.question: What are debits and credits in bookkeeping?
faq.answer: Debits and credits are the two sides of every bookkeeping entry. Debits are recorded on the left side and increase assets and expenses. Credits are recorded on the right side and increase liabilities, equity, and revenue. Every entry must balance.

faq.question: Why do debits and credits need to be equal?
faq.answer: Equal debits and credits enforce the accounting equation: Assets = Liabilities + Equity. If debits and credits don't balance, it means the equation is broken and there is an error in the records that must be found and corrected.
